page: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-16g-4vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine featuring a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 4 GB of VRAM. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is supported by an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance split between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU exhibits weak multi-core performance, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3512.53 and a PassMark CPU score of 3681.75. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers averaging 28.99 GB/sec. However, the fractional NVIDIA A16 GPU delivers strong results in machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier prompt processing speeds of 8765.82 tokens per second for a 135M model and 308.92 tokens per second for a 7B model. Text generation for the 7B model is slower, registering at 7.83 tokens per second.

This instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated computing by partitioning a physical GPU into a smaller, fractional resource. This resource density makes it highly suitable for lightweight LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, and GPU-dependent development environments. Conversely, poor database performance of 1005.99 operations on PassMark and weak multi-core CPU metrics make it unsuitable for heavy database hosting, high-throughput web serving, or intensive CPU-bound parallel processing.
description: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-16g-4vram is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for entry-level parallel processing and machine learning workloads. It features a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 4 GB of VRAM, paired with 2 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and an 80 GB NVMe SSD. While benchmark results show weak multi-core CPU performance and limited memory bandwidth, the instance excels in lightweight machine learning tasks, delivering top-tier prompt processing speeds of 308.92 tokens per second for 7B LLM models. This resource configuration provides a cost-efficient option for developers requiring hardware acceleration without the expense of a full GPU. It is best suited for small-scale LLM inference, model prototyping, and GPU-accelerated development, but is not recommended for database operations or CPU-intensive workloads.
